subject: Liability exposure structuring with service-credit offsets – proposal & asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>, Nimbus Systems Legal <legal@nimbus.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Liability exposure structuring with service-credit offsets – proposal & asks

Hi Aisha / Nimbus team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As promised, Im sending a concise proposal on the liability ceiling mechanics so your legal and procurement teams can review alongside the Order Form redlines. High-level goals we heard: protect Nimbus against catastrophic loss, but keep commercial risk aligned with paid consumption and service reliability.

Proposal (high level):
- Primary liability ceiling: capped at the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid by Nimbus in the preceding 12-month period or (ii) USD 3,000,000 (floor), aggregated across all claims in a 12-month rolling window.
- Service-credit offset: permitted offsets for liability exposure up to 50% of the applicable cap where Redwood has issued formal service credits tied to SLA breaches for the same incident(s). Credits must be documented and applied within 90 days of the incident.
- Per-incident carveouts: No change to standard carveouts for willful misconduct, gross negligence (narrowly defined), or third-party IP indemnity.
- Consequential damage exclusion: Mutual exclusion retained; narrow operational exceptions possible for direct data-loss remediation costs (pre-agreed threshold).

Why credits: For many infra-related disputes, Nimbus prefers that operational remediation (credits/refunds) reduce overall cash exposure instead of duplicative cash damages. This preserves a predictable commercial relationship while keeping an upper bound on Redwoods balance-sheet risk.

Attached: a redline PDF with the MSA section and a clean Order Form draft showing the cap numbers.

Asks: Can your legal team confirm (a) whether the concept of a service-credit offset is acceptable in principle, (b) whether a 50% offset cap is a deal-breaker, and (c) any procurement timing constraints for getting the Order Form signed?

Happy to hop on a short call if that speeds resolution — Im flexible later this week.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Redlines_20261201.pdf (pdf), OrderForm_Nimbus_v3.docx (docx)

From: Aisha Qureshi <aisha.qureshi@nimbus.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>, Nimbus Systems Legal <legal@nimbus.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Liability exposure structuring with service-credit offsets – proposal & asks

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the attachments. I circulated to procurement and our outside counsel. Preliminary feedback:

- Procurement likes the fee-basis approach (ties liability to spend), but they prefer an "annual tranche" view: cap resets each 12-month invoice anniversary rather than a rolling 12-month calculation — helps budgeting.
- Legal is cautious on credit offsets. Our counsels note: any offset that reduces the cash liability should be tightly scoped (e.g., credits only for the specific SLA-related claim and not applied to indemnity claims). They flagged the 50% offset as potentially high; they suggest 25% cap.
- Floor of USD 3M might be too high for our mid-market deployment; procurement requests modeling at USD 1.5M floor and a conditional uplift to 3M after 24 months of committed spend > $X (they asked us to provide the threshold).
- We also need a clear definition and process for how credits are issued and documented (timelines, remedy matrix).

Wed like Redwood legal to propose language that captures the annual-reset alternative, a narrower credit-offset (25%), and the conditional floor uplift. Can your legal team provide two short alternatives we can punt to counsel: (A) rolling 12-month cap (your original), (B) annual tranche (procurement preferred) with identical offsets?

Procurement asked if we can lock pricing for 12 months upon signature; if so, they can expedite the Order Form.

Best,
Aisha
Sr. Sourcing Manager | Nimbus Systems
aisha.qureshi@nimbus.com

--
Nimbus will also attach their suggested redline when counsel is done. Expect delivery by Friday.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Liability exposure structuring with service-credit offsets – internal positions / countermoves

Team — forwarding Nimbus feedback and my quick positions for coordination before we respond.

Summary internal positions:
- We should be flexible on the annual-reset vs rolling; both are acceptable operationally. Recommend we offer both options in the template: default to rolling 12-month (our original) but allow a customer election for annual tranche at signature. This preserves our telemetry assumptions while giving procurement what it wants.
- Service-credit offset: accept in principle but reduce to 33% (compromise between their 25% ask and our 50%). Rationale: credits should meaningfully reduce exposure for recurring operational incidents but not fully erase cash liability. Also require that credits be pre-defined in our SLA appendix and limited to credits for the identical event (ID match).
- Floor / uplift: propose $2,000,000 floor with an auto-uplift to $3,000,000 only if commitment hits a 24-month ARR threshold we can define (e.g., $3.6M TCV). That keeps early-stage deals conservative while aligning with scale.
- Carveouts: keep narrow gross negligence definition and no change to IP indemnity carveouts.

Suggested next steps: 1) Jonas send a short note back to Nimbus acknowledging their asks and proposing the two language alternatives (rolling vs annual) and the 33% offset compromise; 2) loop legal (me) on the redline exchange and schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal review if Nimbus counsel still pushes.

Ill draft two short redline snippets (A/B) for you to attach. Marcus, please prepare a simple fee-model table showing the cap numbers at 6/12/24 months at the $2M/$3M floors so Procurement can see outcomes.

Laura
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: internal_note_liability_positions.txt (text)

Aisha — thanks for the clear feedback and for routing to counsel. Appreciate procurements perspective on the annual tranche. We can move quickly on this one.

What we will send you by EOD tomorrow:
- Two short redline alternatives (Case A: rolling 12-month cap, 50% offset language had been our starting ask but we are revising it to 33% per internal counsel; Case B: annual tranche cap, 33% offset) with precise credit documentation steps and a 90-day documentation window.
- A fee-impact table from Marcus that shows example caps under $1.5M, $2M, and $3M floors plus the conditional uplift mechanics.
- A clean Order Form that will include a 12-month price lock option for procurement to expedite signature.

If Nimbus legal wants a quick legal-to-legal call to settle the narrow offsets/definitions, Laura is available Thursday morning PST; I can coordinate. Otherwise well push the redlines into the DocuSign link and flag the items for counsel to review.
